title: ZPA Go SDK service functions that return partial results, send wrong keys, or reject valid input

prose.text: These are separate defects in individual ZPA SDK service packages and the shared search helpers, not one mechanism. What they share is that the SDK's own helper decides what a caller sees, and the caller cannot tell. Zero-value writes are in [[shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes]], paging is in [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination]], and policy rule ordering (including the `BulkReorder` context defect) is in [[zpa.terraform.rule-order]]. The ZIA counterpart is [[zia.sdk-go.service-defects]].

prose.heading: Partial or incomplete results reported as success

prose.text: {{provisioning-key-api-requires-association-type}} {{provisioning-key-all-associations-fixed-list}} {{provider-provisioning-key-schema-and-importer}} Keys of the two unprobed association types cannot be imported by name or by numeric ID without `association_type` set {{provisioning-key-all-associations-fixed-list|ref}}. Whether keys are stored under those two types, and how the API lists them, is open {{gap:provisioning-key-association-types}}.

prose.heading: Valid input rejected before any request

prose.text: {{assistant-schedule-update-rejects-disabled}} {{provider-schedule-resources-pass-enabled-through}} Whether the API accepts `enabled = false` on a schedule update is open {{gap:schedule-disable-contract}}.
{{query-encoder-emits-plus-for-space}} {{query-encoder-space-as-plus}} How the list search treats `+` versus `%20` and the removed characters is open {{gap:search-filter-semantics}}.
{{policy-update-rule-nil-deref}} {{other-mutators-dereference-unchecked-pointers}} What such a panic does to the provider process is open {{gap:panic-effect}}.

{{openapi-association-enum-includes-unprobed-types}} So the enum does not settle whether provisioning keys are stored under SITE_CONTROLLER_GRP or EXPORTER_GRP {{gap:provisioning-key-association-types}}.

checks.do: Whether a key of one of the two unprobed association types must be managed, by creating it in Terraform, or left unmanaged.
Whether `frequency_interval` is valid before a schedule update, since an empty or invalid value fails the same way as a disabled schedule.
Whether the error reads `cannot update a disabled schedule` before a failed schedule update is attributed to the server.
Whether a lookup by a name containing punctuation failed with `no ... named ... was found`, which points at the search sanitizer.

provisioning-key-all-associations-fixed-.statement: The provisioning-key lookups that do not take an association type (`GetByNameAllAssociations`, `GetByIDAllAssociations`) iterate a fixed SDK list of three association types: CONNECTOR_GRP, SERVICE_EDGE_GRP, NP_ASSISTANT_GRP. They also treat any error from one type's lookup (not only not-found) as a reason to try the next, and return the last attempt's error. A key stored under any other association type cannot be found through these helpers.

provider-schedule-resources-pass-enabled.statement: Both provider assistant-schedule resources declare `enabled` as Optional without a default, copy `d.Get("enabled").(bool)` into the request, and call the SDK update. So `enabled = false`, and an omitted `enabled` (which reads as false), make every update that reaches the SDK update fail there, before its PUT is sent. An empty or invalid `frequency_interval` fails the same way, and a create that finds the schedule already exists falls into this update path; a first create with `enabled = false` can succeed, since create has no such check.

predefined-control-name-escaped-twice.statement: `inspection_predefined_controls.GetByName` applies `url.QueryEscape` to the name and then stores the result with `queryParams.Set`, whose `Encode` escapes it again. A `+` in the name is therefore escaped twice on the wire. The request path re-parses and re-encodes the query but does not undo the first escape.

query-encoder-space-as-plus.statement: `encodeQueryWithSpacesAsPercent20` therefore encodes a space as `+`, not `%20`, and does not do what its name and comment say.
query-encoder-space-as-plus.conditions: Rests on Go standard library behavior, which no captured source states; reproduced with a snippet: `url.QueryEscape("a b+c")` returns `a+b%2Bc`. Whether the ZPA API treats `+` and `%20` the same in a query is server behavior (gap search-filter-semantics); a comment in common.go says `+` works, a comment in zparequests.go says `%20` is required, and neither is verified here.

See zpa.api.provisioning-keys-wire. Whether keys are stored under the two unprobed types remains the open gap provisioning-key-association-types.

provisioning-key-association-types.title: Whether provisioning keys are stored under SITE_CONTROLLER_GRP or EXPORTER_GRP and how the API lists them
provisioning-key-association-types.blocks: telling whether the fixed association list loses real keys or only unused types
provisioning-key-association-types.detail: In a scratch tenant, create a provisioning key with each of the five association types the provider schema accepts, then call the per-type list endpoint for each and record which keys appear.

schedule-disable-contract.title: Whether the ZPA API accepts enabled=false on an assistant schedule update
schedule-disable-contract.blocks: telling whether the SDK check mirrors the API or blocks a valid request
schedule-disable-contract.detail: Send a PUT to the app connector and service edge schedule endpoints with a valid frequency interval and enabled=false in a scratch tenant. Record the status and the schedule's state afterwards.

search-filter-semantics.title: How the ZPA list search treats `name+EQ+` values, `+` versus `%20`, and removed characters
search-filter-semantics.blocks: telling whether the sanitizer and the plus-encoded spaces cause missed lookups
search-filter-semantics.detail: In a scratch tenant, create objects named with a space, `+`, and parentheses. Search each by exact name with `+` and with `%20` for spaces, with and without the characters the SDK strips, and record which requests return the object.

panic-effect.title: Whether a panic in the provider ends the process or becomes a diagnostic
panic-effect.blocks: saying what an operator sees when a nil-pointer panic fires during a plan or apply
panic-effect.detail: Unverified statement: A panic ends the provider process rather than producing a diagnostic. Neither the provider nor the Go SDK calls recover() at the pins, but what the Terraform plugin SDK does with a panic in a resource function is not in a registered source. What would resolve it: a provider test or a run that triggers one of the nil dereferences and records the Terraform output.
